for_us: Parallelise research (it is independent and reads only); serialise what touches the one phone; write each brief with its boundary; spend agents where the value is, and say the cost.
name: Anthropic's orchestrator-worker research
what: A lead agent plans and starts 3-5 workers in parallel, each with its own context, an explicit objective, output format and boundary ('not X - that is another worker's job'); about 15 times the tokens of one agent; worth it only for work that is truly independent and valuable; later guidance argues most systems should have fewer, better-scoped agents.

for_us: Enforce the ways with command hooks on the lab rather than by an agent watching; start sessions from versioned briefs (prompts/); run patrols on a schedule rather than an agent always on.
name: Claude Code: sessions, teams, hooks, schedules
what: Background sessions with cross-session messages (the desktop app), subagents inside one session, experimental agent teams with a shared task list claimed by file lock, worktrees to keep writers apart, hooks that run commands at fixed points (PreToolUse, Stop, SessionStart) and can block - the deterministic way to enforce a rule - and scheduled runs: desktop tasks on the lab, cloud routines, GitHub Actions.

for_us: Our backlog, decisions and session logs in tad/ocoeco data are already the git-kept work state; ocoeco's 'where the drivers stand' is the identity view. Not to adopt: a second tracker beside ocoeco would be one nature under two names. To take: an agent is a name (OCOECO_BY) with a history in the data, and work is small steps that survive a cut-off session.
name: Gas Town and Beads
what: An orchestrator for 20-30 coding agents: work state lives in git as JSON-lines issues (Beads), not in agents' memory; an agent is a persistent identity, not a session; workflows are chains of small issues an agent walks one at a time, so a crash or a full context loses nothing; supervisor roles patrol with backoff; its author says not to use it unless juggling five or more agents daily.

for_us: The same shape fits us, almost one to one: craft-contrib (rules and RFCs, stamped into every AGENTS.md) is creation-guidelines and the practices; craft-common-actions (CI called, not copied) is ocoeco's gather and the package conveyor's workflows; craft-launcher (installs and updates every app) is the package conveyor's Alpine repository to come; craft-repo-status-app and craft-wiki are the face and docs; every app agent-ready (CLI, JSON control, MCP) is devlab mcp and agent access. What they have and we lack: craft-skills - procedures shared as agent skills, discoverable by every agent rather than remembered (our oco-work words, as skills); and *-corpus repositories - reference data an oracle compares against (for a phone: what Android does on the same hardware - sleep current, audio levels, sensor readings - measured once and kept). Worth taking too: claim before work, estimates in agent-hours, a ranked gaps list and scorecard drawn from data, and the lesson that breadth is fast and only an oracle keeps the numbers honest.
name: ArtCraft: seventeen apps, one organisation
what: Seven, then thirteen clean-room Rust apps built with about 8 parallel Claude agents, each owning one subsystem directory. House rules kept once (craft-contrib/standards) and stamped into every repository's AGENTS.md with a checksum; CI shared from one actions repository; agents check an issue and claim it before working; a generated scorecard, ranked gaps list and parity checklists say what is left; a test oracle (Photoshop's own renders, a CPU compositor for the GPU one) decides what counts as progress; remaining work estimated in agent-hours.

for_us: Android's own measure of a phone; our proofs are named checks of the same smallness, and we keep not-needed and not known yet apart where it counts an ignored case as a pass.
name: Android Compatibility Test Suite
what: The compatibility tests a phone passes to count as Android: module, case, method, run per device and build, pass, fail or not executed.

for_us: Replaces our hand-made waiting-to-probe checks with the established tool.
name: bootrr
what: Checks that every expected driver probed on a booted device; packaged in pmaports for the CI hook.

for_us: The gateway our lab machine could become, instead of growing its own.
name: CI-tron
what: A bare-metal testing gateway: deploys test environments to devices, sequences power and boot, collects logs; devices are trained through boot cycles before they take jobs.

for_us: Its scope is the list a native mainline phone must replace, the hardest first: our phone stages follow the same areas.
name: Halium
what: Reuses the Android vendor HALs (radio, audio, camera, media, sensors, GNSS, Wi-Fi, vibrator, fingerprint) through libhybris so a phone runs a Linux userspace.

for_us: Consumes mainline device support rather than building it: surya reaches Mobian through mainline and a family recipe, after pmOS.
name: mobian-recipes
what: Debian images built with debos; devices grouped in families by SoC; device packages (<device>-tweaks); weekly CI image builds. Points to the postmarketOS wiki to judge whether a device runs mainline.

for_us: Our device.toml derives from deviceinfo and adds only what it lacks (how the lab reaches the phone), rather than duplicating it.
name: Device packages and deviceinfo
what: Each device package carries a deviceinfo file - codename, name, architecture, flash method, device tree - the device's manifest.

for_us: Our lab is a one-phone version of it. Aim: surya as a device under test in their farm, our tests in their shape - contributed, not kept apart.
name: postmarketOS hardware CI
what: Tests on real phones: CI-tron as the testing gateway, power units that switch devices and press buttons, GitLab pipelines generated per device from a template in its package; scaling toward a farm of dozens of devices (talk at the 2026 conference).

for_us: Our automatic checks and the test kernel's timeout hook belong in this shape, so they can go upstream and run in their CI.
name: Initramfs CI hook and test packages
what: postmarketos-mkinitfs-hook-ci runs tests inside the initramfs; tests ship as small subpackages that install themselves for the right device (postmarketos-test-suspend, -unl0kr).

for_us: The only stage order the world keeps as data. We take its gating as goal steps (daily-usable-phone), not its weights or percent, and keep its ticks apart from proofs.
name: UBports device data
what: devices.ubuntu-touch.io keeps, per device, feature ticks in nine categories, each category gating a progress stage (booting, core connectivity, essential, fully optimised, never caps).
